country_benchmark_source.conversion: Published numeric cell divided by 1000; no geographic allocation or forecast extrapolation.
country_benchmark_source.methodology_section: About the Benefit expenditure by Country and Region tables
country_benchmark_source.scope: Combined State Pension expenditure for residents of each named country. The source separately lists overseas/unknown; no overseas share is allocated here. DWP estimates geographic expenditure from National Statistics caseload and average payments applied to total outturn.

unavailable.GB_by_type: Overseas expenditure/caseload are separated only for all State Pension types together.
unavailable.by_age: No State Pension age-band expenditure/caseload table in this workbook.
unavailable.by_geography: No country/region State Pension forecast table in this workbook.
unavailable.after_2030: No verified published long-term spending benchmark supplied.

coverage.geography_note: GB totals exclude overseas State Pension. Basic/new GB benchmarks remain unavailable because the workbook separates overseas only for their combined total.

support_audit.scope: Completed archived-source coverage audit and/or existing central national full-run support, as applicable. Per-path audits of national totals were stopped before completion as a scope cut: national fiscal totals draw on thousands of records, so per-path audits of them add nothing. This does not certify the model/data pair.

retained_replay_comparison.comparison: independent full runs with absolute float tolerance
retained_replay_comparison.scope: Central Enhanced FRS UK/GB gross and net in 2034 and 2039. Historical paired means and SEs are retained, not independently replayed.

historical_part_d.interpretation: retained historical part D full-run aggregates; not recalculated or scaled

method: Each figure comes from full PolicyEngine UK runs of both rules. The central path and the original 40 Microcosm-paired macro indices run on Enhanced FRS for every treatment. Contrasts are calculated within paths, then estimated using the original stratum masses and both Monte Carlo variance components. No output scaling.
